claims.statement: `Institution.csv_format` on `account_institutions` is a comma-separated positional template string mapping each column of a broker CSV export to a standardized placeholder, and it is the only per-broker configuration the generic parser consumes — there is no broker-specific branching in `src/account/csv/parser.py`.

`normalize_token` is the single normalization rule applied to both template tokens and file headers — it strips a leading UTF-8 BOM and whitespace, unwraps `{...}`, lowercases, and collapses non-alphanumeric runs into single underscores — so real-world broker labels only match the template through the `HEADER_ALIASES` table.

`header_matches` accepts a header alias match in either direction (actual in `HEADER_ALIASES[expected]` or expected in `HEADER_ALIASES[actual]`), which is what lets a `{type}` template token line up with a file column labeled `Security Type`.

Header validation is two-stage and strictly positional: a raw column-count mismatch raises `CsvHeaderCountMismatchError` before any name comparison, and the first element-wise name mismatch raises `CsvHeaderColumnMismatchError` with a 1-based column index; a reordered export therefore fails even when every label is recognized.

`map_account_type` lowercases and trims the raw account type and resolves only the documented `ACCOUNT_TYPE_MAP` keys (TFSA/RRSP/SPOUSAL_RRSP/FHSA variants plus non-registered/personal/margin) to `AccountTypeEnum`; an unrecognized value raises `CsvUnsupportedAccountTypeError` (a `CsvRowValidationError`) and aborts the entire parse rather than skipping the row.

`_parse_position` treats quantity and book value asymmetrically: an unparseable quantity raises `CsvInvalidQuantityError` (and a missing quantity cell silently parses as `Decimal("0")`), while an unparseable book value is swallowed into `None` so a malformed cost basis degrades to unknown cost instead of failing the import.

`calculate_average_cost` returns `None` for non-positive quantity or missing book value, otherwise quantizes `book_value / quantity` to 4 decimal places with `ROUND_HALF_UP`; that quantize step fixes every CSV-imported `average_cost` and cascades into all downstream cost-basis P&L.

`GenericCsvParser.parse` enforces per-row invariants while grouping by `account_number`: every row needs a non-empty account number (`CsvMissingAccountNumberError`), but only the first row seen for a new account number needs a non-empty account type (`CsvMissingAccountTypeError`); accounts are returned in first-seen order with `row_idx` reported as a 1-based file line number starting at 2.

Row filtering runs before the quantity parse in `_parse_position`: cash rows and option rows are dropped before `Decimal(...)` is applied, so a filtered row can never raise `CsvInvalidQuantityError`. `is_cash_row` returns False first for a `security_type` of `exchange_traded_fund`/`etf`/`equity`/`stock`/`mutual_fund`, and otherwise flags a row as cash when the symbol is empty or `cash`/`cad`/`usd`, the security type is `cash`/`currency`, or the symbol starts with `sec-c-`; `is_option_row` flags `option`/`derivative` security types or OCC-pattern symbols. Options are defended a second time in `sync_account_csv_positions` via `is_option_symbol`.

The parser's exception taxonomy is rooted at `CsvParserError` with three branches — `CsvHeaderValidationError` (count/column), `CsvEmptyError` (empty content, empty template, no columns; plus the service-level `CsvFileEmptyError` subclass), and `CsvRowValidationError` (unsupported account type, missing account number, missing account type, invalid quantity) — and the router maps `CsvParserError` to HTTP 400 with the message as `detail`.

All three CSV endpoints (`POST /accounts/csv/inspect`, `/accounts/csv/import`, `/accounts/{account_id}/csv-sync`) share one gate: `CsvAccountService.validate_csv_institution` raises `InstitutionNotFoundError` (404) when the institution row is missing and `CsvImportDisabledError` (400) when `csv_import_enabled` is false OR `csv_format` is empty, so `csv_import_enabled=True` with `csv_format=None` behaves identically to a disabled institution.

`inspect_csv` parses, then when a `user_id` is given it marks `exists = True` and overwrites each discovered account's `currency` with the stored `Account.currency` and its `net_deposits` with the stored value for account numbers the user already has at that institution (matched on `external_id` plus `institution_id`); `exists` drives the modal's `Update holdings` versus `Create account` badge and the `Still correct?` net-deposits hint.

`import_accounts` filters parsed accounts against the requested `account_numbers` and raises `NoMatchingAccountsInCsvError` when the intersection is empty — there is no import-everything mode. `CsvAccountDuplicateError` is mapped to 400 by the router but is never raised on this path: a requested number that already exists is treated as an in-place update returning the same account id.

Accounts created by CSV import are stamped `api_sync_enabled=False` (with `integration_user_id=None`), which is what makes `POST /accounts/{account_id}/sync` reject them with 400 `API sync is not enabled for account {id}` and makes the frontend account-row refresh control render `Update from CSV` instead of `Sync positions`.

Currency resolution at import has a defined precedence per account: the caller-supplied `account_currencies[number]` (trimmed and uppercased) wins, then the parsed account currency, then `"CAD"`; for an existing account a difference triggers `AccountRepository.update_currency`, and for a new account it becomes the `AccountSchema.currency`.

`sync_account_from_csv` is asymmetric with import: it never creates an account, never changes the account currency, cannot clear stored net deposits, and never considers other discovered accounts in the file — it matches only the target account's `external_id` (raising `AccountNotInCsvError` otherwise), validates the account's own institution's CSV enablement, writes `free_cash` via `update_free_cash`, applies the caller's `net_deposits` only when a value was supplied, and is the only CSV endpoint that enforces account ownership (404 for another user's account).

`sync_account_csv_positions` is the shared tail for all three paths: it resolves each symbol through `SecurityApi.get_or_create_from_broker` (wrapping a `ValueError` from the market layer as `SecurityResolutionError`, which the router maps to 400), then writes via `PositionApi.create` — which replaces every position row for the account — or calls `sync_by_account(account_id, [])` when the resolved list is empty, so an all-cash export clears the account instead of leaving stale rows; finally it stamps `update_last_sync_at`.

Security resolution for CSV positions is institution-scoped and cached through `SecurityBroker` rows: a repeat `(institution, broker_symbol, broker_exchange)` short-circuits to the mapped security, and a new pair maps the broker symbol/exchange to an EODHD query (`TSX`→`TO`, `CSE`→`CA`, `NYSE`/`NASDAQ`→`US`, `.`→`-`), searches the cached gateway, creates or reuses the security, primes its latest close, and records the raw search results.

The CSV endpoints accept their parameters as either multipart form fields or query parameters sharing the same alias (form wins): inspect takes `institution_id`, and import takes `institution_id`, `account_numbers`, `currencies` and `net_deposits`. `institution_id` and `account_numbers` are mandatory (422) and account numbers accept a JSON list string, a comma-separated string, or repeated values and are deduplicated in order; a malformed `currencies` JSON is silently ignored, while `net_deposits` is parsed strictly and returns 422 for malformed JSON, non-object payloads or non-numeric values. csv-sync takes only the file plus an optional numeric `net_deposits` form field, with no query alias.
None of the three CSV endpoints carries a rate limit — only `POST /accounts/{account_id}/sync` is decorated with `@limiter.limit("3/minute")` in `src/account/router.py`.

All three CSV endpoints decode the upload with `content_bytes.decode("utf-8-sig")`, so a UTF-8 BOM never reaches the parser and a read/decode failure produces an HTTP 400 rather than an unhandled 500; the parser additionally strips a leading BOM defensively.

`WEALTHSIMPLE_CSV_FORMAT` in `src/commands/seed.py` is the worked example of the template contract: 21 placeholders in Wealthsimple column order, seeded onto the `WEALTHSIMPLE` institution with `csv_import_enabled=True` and re-asserted on every seed run for an already-existing institution, so a template change reaches an existing database.

Onboarding a new broker CSV export is a data change, not a code change: set `csv_format` to the positional template matching the export header and `csv_import_enabled = True`; parser code only needs touching when the export requires placeholder vocabulary the parser does not consume or a header label no alias covers. The caveat is that templates omitting `{account_number}` or `{account_type}` fail at runtime with the row-level missing errors, and omitting `{quantity}` silently yields zero-quantity positions.

The institution seam surfaces to the frontend through `GET /integration/institutions`, which returns `csv_import_enabled` and `csv_format`; the import modal filters that list to `csv_import_enabled === true` and auto-selects the broker when exactly one remains, so adding a second CSV broker requires no frontend change.

`import-account-csv-modal.svelte` is a two-step dialog (broker+file, then a preview table) with client-side `.csv`-extension and 10 MB size guards that disable the primary button, an empty-account-list error that keeps the user on step 1, all discovered accounts selected by default with select-all/indeterminate header state, a per-row currency dropdown plus a per-row `Net deposits` input, and `Back` preserving the broker and file.

`update-account-csv-modal.svelte` is a single-step dialog that sends only the file plus an optional `{ netDeposits }` option for one account to `syncAccountCsv(account.id, file, { netDeposits })` — no institution or account number travels in the body, and a blank input omits the field so the stored value is left unchanged (the modal cannot clear it); it is owned by `accounts-list-item.svelte` through a `ModalState`, opened from the account-row refresh control that renders `Update from CSV` when `api_sync_enabled` is false.

`AccountClient.importAccountsCsv`'s fourth parameter and `syncAccountCsv`'s third parameter are overloaded slots typed `Options | string | null`: an options object becomes form fields while a string is routed to the auth token. The import client sends repeated `account_numbers` fields plus `currencies` and `net_deposits` JSON strings only when those maps are non-empty, and the sync client appends `net_deposits` as a plain string only when it is a non-null number (`undefined` and `null` are both skipped).

Both CSV modals render the backend `detail` string verbatim in a destructive alert, so the parser's diagnostic messages (column index, expected and actual header names, row index, symbol, account type) are what end users actually read.

Focused CSV coverage is layered: `tests/account/csv/test_parser.py` pins the template/alias/filter/rounding contract, `tests/services/test_csv_account_service.py` pins the institution gate and the create/update/sync branches with mocked repositories and `SecurityApi`, `tests/routers/test_csv_inspect.py` and `tests/routers/test_csv_account_endpoints.py` drive the real FastAPI app against Postgres asserting status codes and `PositionModel` rows, and `tests/commands/test_seed.py` pins the seeded template plus seed idempotency.

Cash rows are not dropped from the parse: `GenericCsvParser.parse` diverts them through `_parse_cash_amount` (first non-empty of `quantity`, `market_value`, `book_value`, `book_value_cad`, `book_value_market`, with `,` and `$` stripped) into a per-account running total that is rounded to 2 decimals and emitted as `CsvDiscoveredAccount.free_cash`, while still contributing no position.

The service persists the parsed cash balance on all three write branches — an explicit `AccountRepository.update_free_cash` call for an existing account during import and for the csv-sync target, and the `free_cash` field of the `AccountSchema` for a newly created account — and that repository method assigns the column outright, so `free_cash` is overwritten from the file on every import or sync rather than accumulated across runs.

Net deposits never come from the CSV itself: there is no `{net_deposits}` placeholder in `csv_format`, the parser emits every `CsvDiscoveredAccount` with `net_deposits = None`, `inspect_csv` only copies the already-stored `Account.net_deposits` for accounts the user has at that institution, and therefore every value the service writes originates from user input in a modal.

Import applies net deposits per matching account only for keys present in the `net_deposits` JSON map (on both the existing-account and the new-account branch, after the create); an explicit `null` clears the stored column through `update_net_deposits`, while an omitted key leaves the previous value untouched.

`_parse_net_deposits` is deliberately stricter than the neighbouring `currencies` parser: malformed JSON, a non-object payload, or a non-numeric value produces HTTP 422 instead of being silently dropped, because a dropped amount would quietly change the account's profit/loss basis.

csv-sync writes net deposits only when the optional numeric `net_deposits` form field is present, so a sync that omits it leaves the stored value unchanged and the endpoint offers no way to clear it — only import with an explicit `null` can.

The import modal's `Net deposits` column pre-fills existing accounts from the inspected value with a `Still correct?` hint: a typed number is sent, clearing a pre-filled value sends `{accountNumber: null}`, a never-set new account omits the key, unselected accounts are excluded, negative values are allowed, and a non-numeric entry shows an inline error that disables import.

The update modal pre-fills its `Net deposits` input from `account.net_deposits` when it opens and sends `netDeposits: undefined` for a blank or cleared input, which the client omits from the request body so the backend leaves the stored value unchanged.

A stored net-deposits value changes an account's profit/loss basis: totals and holdings then report `basis = "net_deposits"` and divide profit/loss by net deposits instead of position cost, which is why the CSV modals collect the value and the account row labels its cost basis `Net deposits`.
